To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the subseasonal predictability and predictability skill of the NAO are dominated by linearly independent, low-dimensional, and largely predictable subspace(s) that can be identified by an LIM.

1) subseasonal NAM/NAO forecasts are most skillful when the tropical troposphere, the lower stratosphere, and the upper stratospheric polar vortex are all in a particular state, and 2) the LIM provides a practical tool to identify those events that are predictable.

the subseasonal predictability skill of the North Atlantic oscillation is due to the joint variability between the tropical troposphere (sea-surface temperature) and the lower and upper stratosphere, and the downward propagation from the stratosphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new tools for improving the skill of subseasonal forecasts, which will be of interest to both forecasters and the scientific community.
the identification and understanding of the physical processes underlying subseasonal predictability, which is essential for the improvement of the operational forecast systems.
the predictability of the winter NAO on subseasonal timescales, and we find that the NAO is predictable when the tropical troposphere is warm and the lower stratosphere is cold.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LIM is able to capture the main physical mechanisms responsible for NAO predictability and that this predictability is related to the tropical troposphere-lower stratospheric variability.
the LIM is an effective tool to predict the NAO on subseasonal timescales.

subseasonal NAM/NAO skill is associated with the linear superposition and subsequent downward propagation of two modes of variability that are largely responsible for total NAO variance: tropical SST and lower stratospheric variability, and downward propagating stratospheric variability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
subseasonal skill in predicting the NAO is possible when there is a combination of a strong upper stratospheric polar vortex, a strong lower stratosphere polar vortex and a strong El Nino.
the subseasonal NAM can be skillfully predicted by the LIM and that the LIM provides an effective way of identifying the potentially predictable NAM events.

subseasonal NAM predictability stems from a combination of the stratosphere and tropical troposphere, and that the predictability can be captured by a small set of modes that are relatively easy to identify and diagnose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subseasonal NAM is predictable, but only in certain situations.
the LIM can be used to diagnose and predict subseasonal NAM skill, and to identify those NAM events that are predictable and potentially useful for operational forecasts.

, despite the NAO’s high intrinsic predictability and its strong association with weather extremes, subseasonal predictability is low and sporadic, and is only likely when a few dynamical modes with relatively low total variance are active.
